en: The blue whale is the largest animal on Earth, weighing up to 150,000 kilograms, which equals the mass of about thirty elephants.
Bamboo is the fastest-growing plant on Earth, with some species growing up to 91 centimeters in just a single day.
The human body produces about two million new red blood cells every single second to replace old ones.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird, reaching diving speeds of over 389 kilometers per hour.
The coco de mer plant produces the largest seeds in the world, with each seed weighing up to 42 kilograms.
A human baby is born with about 270 bones, but adults only have 206 because many bones fuse together.
A blue whale's heart beats about ten times per minute, while a tiny mouse's heart beats 500 times per minute.
The Mariana snailfish is the deepest-living fish ever discovered, found at a depth of 8,178 meters in the Pacific Ocean.
The Greenland shark is the longest-living vertebrate, with individuals living for at least 272 years in the cold Arctic waters.
The Rafflesia arnoldii produces the largest individual flower on Earth, measuring up to one meter across and weighing 11 kilograms.
If uncoiled, the DNA inside a single human cell would stretch about two meters long, much longer than you are tall.
The horned dung beetle can pull up to 1,141 times its own body weight, making it the strongest insect on Earth.
